S1.rationale: The installed Codex cell owns source/tool actions, and first-party Task Bridge, verified checkpoints and persistent outcome/task identity preserve useful work across sessions. No current main native issue was identified that demonstrates broken S1 continuity.

S2.rationale: Project/outcome membership and storage file locks protect bookkeeping but not competing Codex task scopes, so the S2 inter-S1 overlap relation remains absent. No independently supported write-collision incident or user-requested conflict contract justifies a new feature.

S3.rationale: Human parent owns current work-priority and outcome lifecycle decisions through Focus/Board, exact task membership and next-action state. The first-party S3=P mechanism is existing product behavior, not a reason to introduce an unauthorized autonomous project manager.

S3*.rationale: Self-reported checkpoint facts can be viewed alongside app history or health, but no independent correctness auditor returns judgments into current task control. Without a reported false completion incident or accepted review policy, there is no justified native audit patch.

S4.rationale: Optional Slack monitoring, schedule intent and update/status checks are signals about existing tasks, without prospective outside-environment strategy generation/adoption. No product-native evidence calls for a separate S4 adaptation owner.

S5.rationale: Identity registry, explicit user intent and permission to write to connected services are ordinary authority/admission controls, not ultimate identity policy deliberation. No first-party S5 mandate is established, nor a necessary product change.
